tasks.short: Build the weekly HR numbers pack for the sites and the board

today.trigger: A site manager, HR business partner, the HR Director or the works council asks for numbers, or the Monday or month-end pack is due.
steps: Check that the nightly AFAS extract has refreshed in Power BI, then note the refresh time.
Reconcile headcount, joiners, leavers and verzuim hours to AFAS for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Split own staff from flex, warehouse from office, and the transport CAO from the warehouse CAO.
Build or adjust the Power BI page or the Excel copy, apply the minimum group size, and write a short note.
Send it by Outlook or Teams and file a copy on SharePoint.
drudgery: Re-checking the same totals after every refresh
Copying AFAS figures into Excel because a filter is wrong
Removing names and absence reasons from an export before it can be shared
Rebuilding one pack in three layouts for the HR Director, a site manager and the works council
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes to reconciliation and reformatting. A site that counts flex workers in headcount while payroll counts them out can take half a day to untangle.

lenses.faster: The Monday pack and the month-end pack publish after the nightly refresh passes its checks, so the export, the pivot and the reformat drop out of the morning.
lenses.autonomous: A clean refresh delivers the standard pack to the fixed audience. A failed check or a broken refresh opens an item for the analyst before the site handover.
lenses.ambitious: Every site manager and every night-shift handover gets the same verzuim, hiring, 90-day and certificate view each week, and the works-council pack is ready when the agenda is set. The North Star inputs are reported properly, from one definition, for the first time.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing totals across Excel copies. What remains is judging a real movement, such as a Tilburg night-shift absence spike or a cohort that is gone before day 90.
lenses.options: A custom question returns five cuts from the same approved measures: site, contract type, shift, tenure band and staffing agency.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the metric catalogue, the privacy rules and the tests, and reviews breaks, and the weekly rebuild becomes a run of that system.
reach: Payroll Specialist: the joiners, leavers and wage-component check before the monthly pay lock
FP&A Analyst: the labour-cost bridge from headcount to the general ledger
Learning and Development Specialist: the forklift, VCA and food-safety expiry list from Studytube
Recruiter: the time-to-hire and stage-aging report from Recruitee

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a movement is real or a coding error, and what may be shown to a site manager or the works council when absence could identify a person.
tasks.pattern_why: The packs use fixed definitions and a structured AFAS extract. Each total either matches payroll or the check fails, so the run is ordinary software.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract lands, or a manager asks a question that already maps to a catalogue measure.
steps: Refresh the Power BI model and reconcile headcount, joiners, leavers and verzuim hours to AFAS for each site.
Apply the agreed minimum group size and keep absence reason and health fields out of every management view.
Publish the standard pack with row-level security: a site sees its own site, HR and Finance see all three.
For a custom ask, return only catalogue measures and log the definition and the population used.
Hold the pack when a check fails or the question needs a new definition.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases a failed check, approves a new metric definition, and signs off the works-council pack before it is sent.
data_needed: Nightly AFAS HR and payroll extract
Site, contract type, CAO and own-staff versus flex flags
Verzuim hours and the payroll population they reconcile to
Agreed minimum group size and the distribution list
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR analytics log: refresh id, reconciliation differences, definition used, and who received the pack.

evidence.claim: Power BI can refresh a dataset on a schedule and deliver a report to a set audience.
AFAS Profit holds the contracts, absence and payroll records these packs have to match.
Works councils receive periodic personnel information, so a shared pack has to be accurate and agreed in scope.
Absence figures shown for a small team can identify a person, so management packs use aggregates and a minimum group size.

risks: Blending the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO, or own staff and flex, produces a verzuim rate the works council will reject.
A custom export pulls an absence reason or a named employee into a site manager's file.
The nightly extract misses a same-day joiner or leaver, and the site corrects it in Excel, so two versions circulate.
Flex hours sit in three agency portals as well as in AFAS, so headcount depends on which source was used.
research_questions: What share of report requests repeats a catalogue metric, and what share asks for a new definition?
Can headcount, leavers and verzuim hours reconcile automatically to AFAS for each site?
Which packs does the works council already receive, and which fields have they objected to?
How often is a published number corrected after a site manager replies?

tasks.short: Get the right HR numbers to the right people on time

today.trigger: Someone arrives at a meeting without the number they needed, or the analyst remembers who usually asks before payroll lock or a works-council prep.
steps: Keep a private list of who wants which report and on which day.
Check the refresh, then export or screenshot the page.
Mail it or post it in Teams, often as Excel so the recipient can filter.
Answer the reply that the filter was wrong or that the file shows too much.
Hear after the meeting that the night-shift supervisor never saw the mail.
drudgery: Resending a file that went to the wrong list
Remembering the audience from one month to the next
Deleting columns by hand so a site does not see another site's pay data
Chasing read receipts before payroll locks
today.time_sinks: The time goes to the audience, the file format and the deadline. The chart itself is already built. Payroll lock, the works-council agenda and the Monday shift handover do not wait.

lenses.faster: Row-level security and a fixed calendar replace the per-person export. Each person opens one pack, already limited to their site and role.
lenses.autonomous: A successful refresh before the deadline delivers the pack. A late or failed refresh posts a short warning to the analyst and the recipient before the meeting starts.
lenses.ambitious: Each value stream has a beat that already exists when the meeting opens: hire-to-productive on Monday, verzuim and Poortwachter status every week, the pay-cycle pack three working days before lock, and the works-council pack on the consultation cycle.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses maintaining the mailing list. People still want a figure that is present at the shift handover and at the payroll meeting.
lenses.options: One approved metric goes out as a site tile, a board one-pager and a works-council appendix from the same refresh.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the audience, the deadline and the access rule, and tends the exceptions. Delivery itself runs on the calendar.
reach: Payroll Specialist: the pre-lock reminder with headcount and new wage components
Controller: the labour-cost flash on the same population finance will book
Learning and Development Specialist: the Monday certificate-expiry nudge to the site
Recruiter: the stale-vacancy nudge to the hiring manager

tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a new audience may see a field, especially absence, pay, flex names, or anything sent to a staffing agency or the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Audience, weekday, dataset and grain are rules. The check is simple: the right role saw the right grain on time, and a raw employee file did not go out.

in_practice.trigger: A dataset refresh succeeds, a pack deadline falls inside the next working day, or a refresh fails inside that window.
steps: Tie each pack to a deadline: Monday site handover, three working days before payroll lock, and the works-council agenda date.
Deliver through Power BI row-level security so Tilburg sees Tilburg, and wages stay with HR, payroll and finance.
Post a one-line Teams note when the pack is late or a check failed, naming the metric and the site.
Send a link to the app. Keep employee numbers and absence reasons out of wide mail attachments.
Log delivery, failed refreshes, and any forward outside the tenant.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves a new recipient, any external recipient, and any pack that adds a field.
data_needed: Recipient role and site from AFAS
Pack calendar aligned to payroll lock and works-council dates
Row-level security rules
Dataset refresh status
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint delivery log: pack name, audience, timestamp, refresh id, and failures.

evidence.claim: Power BI row-level security and app audiences can limit a report to a site or a role.
Power Automate can start a flow when a Power BI dataset refresh completes and post to Teams or Outlook.
Emailing employee-level HR extracts to a wide internal list is a recurring AVG incident pattern.

risks: A site manager forwards a file to a staffing agency and flex names or rates leave the company.
An AFAS department change breaks row-level security and Venlo sees Rotterdam wage data.
The pack arrives at 07:00 by mail and the night shift still works from a printed handover.
The works council receives a management pack that was never agreed as their information set.
research_questions: Which packs have a hard deadline, such as payroll lock, the 42-week UWV notification or a works-council meeting, and which are habit?
Can every recipient be mapped to an AFAS site and role?
What was forwarded or downloaded last quarter, and did any file leave the tenant?
Do night-shift supervisors use Teams, mail or a printed handover, and at what time?

tasks.short: Keep the HR dashboards and the AFAS data model correct

today.trigger: AFAS is updated, a CAO wage component changes, a certificate type appears in Studytube, or a manager spots a wrong tile.
steps: Hear about the break from payroll, HR admin or a site manager.
Find the field in the nightly extract and in the Power BI model.
Patch the measure or the Excel bridge and check a handful of employees by hand.
Update the live page and reply to the person who noticed.
Leave the definition note unfinished in a personal file.
drudgery: Hunting which copy of a measure is the live one
Hand-checking employee numbers after a small AFAS change
Rewriting the same flex-versus-own-staff filter on every page
Decoding site codes and agency names that differ per source
today.time_sinks: Finding the broken field and proving the fix against AFAS takes the time. The design conversation is the short part.

lenses.faster: The analyst gets a drafted measure change, a reconciliation query and a change note, and spends the time on the check and the definition.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly test flags a broken key, a new AFAS wage component or an unknown Studytube certificate code on the morning it appears.
lenses.ambitious: Time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, verzuim and certificate compliance each have one written definition, one owner and a test that fails in the open.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the field hunt. The work people want to keep is agreeing what Noordhaven means by productive at day 90 and which hours count as verzuim.
lenses.options: A definition change arrives as three drafts, new measure, new column or a payroll mapping table, each with a site-level reconciliation beside it.
lenses.altitude: The analyst runs the model as a small product: tests, a change log and a release. Pages get fixed by changing that system.
reach: Payroll Specialist: mapping a new CAO allowance or ploegentoeslag into the extract
HR Administrator: the field-entry rules that keep the extract clean
Finance Controller: the labour-cost categories that must match the ledger
Learning and Development Specialist: the certificate code list for forklift, VCA and food safety

tasks.human_edge: Agreeing the definition with payroll, the HR Director and, where the figure monitors staff, the works council. A wrong verzuim definition that ships on its own does more harm than a slow correction.
tasks.pattern_why: The model is shared, the definitions are agreed with payroll and the HR Director, and a bad release lands in the works-council pack. AI drafts the change. The analyst owns the model.

in_practice.trigger: A reconciliation test fails, AFAS or Studytube adds a code, or payroll announces a CAO component change.
steps: Read the failed test and name the field that moved.
Draft the model change and a before-and-after reconciliation for each site and each contract type.
Put the written definition next to the draft: population, flex in or out, which CAO.
The analyst edits the draft in a workspace copy and reruns the tests.
Publish after the tests pass and write the change in the SharePoint log the same day.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst publishes every live change. A definition that changes an OR figure or a pay figure also needs the metric owner, the HR Director or the Payroll Specialist.
data_needed: Current Power BI model and the AFAS field list
Test employees for each site, CAO and contract type
CAO wage-component list from payroll
Studytube certificate codes
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint model change log: date, field, definition, test result, and who published.

evidence.claim: Assistants can draft SQL and DAX from a described measure, and the analyst still validates the result against source totals.
A scheduled check that compares model totals to the source extract will catch a broken key or a new code.
AFAS Profit is the system whose field changes force HRIS model maintenance.

risks: A drafted measure matches Rotterdam and drops night-shift allowances or flex workers in Venlo.
Two verzuim definitions stay live, one in the dashboard and one in payroll.
A draft fills a missing employee attribute with a plausible value. The rule is that only source fields are used.
A staff-monitoring metric changes and the works council hears about it after the page is live.
research_questions: How many dashboard breaks in the last six months came from an AFAS change, a definition dispute or a failed refresh?
Is there a separate workspace, or do edits land on the app people already use?
Which measures do payroll and HR already calculate differently?
Does the nightly extract document field names and effective dates?

tasks.short: Answer why a dashboard number does not match AFAS

today.trigger: An HR business partner, site manager, recruiter or payroll specialist messages the analyst that a tile looks wrong.
steps: Ask which page, which site and which date they mean.
Open Power BI and AFAS and try to reproduce the filter.
Check the usual causes: flex in or out, refresh time, department code, row-level security, certificate name.
Reply in Teams with the reason and often a corrected Excel.
See the same question next week from another site.
drudgery: Answering the same causes: flex, refresh time, site code, FTE versus heads, certificate name
Long Teams threads made of filter screenshots
Rebuilding a user's Excel so they can check the tile
Being the only person who can explain a blank tile
today.time_sinks: The back-and-forth to learn which number they mean takes as long as the lookup. A logged definition would answer most of those questions on the first reply.

lenses.faster: The first reply already shows the definition, the refresh time and the AFAS total beside the tile, so the filter interview drops away for known causes.
lenses.autonomous: A repeated known cause returns the saved explanation as soon as it is asked. The analyst sees the questions that match no known cause.
lenses.ambitious: Every tile carries a plain definition and a compare-to-AFAS path, so site managers can use the Monday pack in the handover and trust it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the screenshot thread. The part worth keeping is the odd case: a real data error, or a manager who is asking for a decision.
lenses.options: The reply shows the figure with flex in, with flex out, and for office staff only, so the manager can see why their own total differed.
lenses.altitude: The analyst fixes the tile, the on-page definition or the refresh alert that caused the ticket, and the same question stops arriving one manager at a time.
reach: HR Administrator: AFAS entry questions that are really missing field rules
Payroll Specialist: which employees sit in this pay run and why
Recruiter: what a Recruitee stage name means in the time-to-hire measure

tasks.human_edge: The manager who is pushing back on a target, a verzuim case or a hire that failed. That is a conversation, and a drafted data reply will miss it.
tasks.pattern_why: The analyst stays in the conversation with the manager. AI prepares the comparison and the likely cause. The analyst decides what to say, because a wrong cause gets repeated in a shift handover.

in_practice.trigger: A Teams or mail question about a tile, or the same question appearing twice in a month.
steps: Pull the page, the user's site and role, the refresh time and the catalogue definition.
Compare the tile to the AFAS total for that population.
Draft a short reply with the definition, the two totals and the likely cause.
The analyst edits the reply and sends it.
When the same cause repeats, change the tile or the definition text so the question ends.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst sends every reply that states a number. A saved explanation for a known cause goes out on its own only after the analyst has approved that text once.
data_needed: The question text
The asker's role and site
Refresh log and metric catalogue
AFAS totals for the same population
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint support log: question, cause, reply date, and whether the tile or the definition was changed.

evidence.claim: Power BI can show the dataset refresh time, and a report page can display the written measure definition.
A large share of HR dashboard questions repeat a small set of filter and population causes.
Recruitee and Studytube have their own reports, so some mismatches are a second source of truth.

risks: A drafted cause is wrong and a site manager acts on it before anyone corrects it.
The reply shows a wage or an absence detail to a role that should see only the site aggregate.
Support volume is bursty around month-end, and a bot built for a steady queue costs more than it saves.
Managers start bargaining with the explanation and ignore the agreed definition.
research_questions: How many support messages arrive in a normal month, and what share are the same five causes?
Do questions come through a shared channel or through the analyst's personal chat?
Which wrong answers would still be costly if a manager believed them for a week?
Is the load spread across the month or concentrated on payroll lock and works-council weeks?

tasks.short: Watch which clients and seasons drive hiring and flex hours

today.trigger: A site says volume is up, an agency invoice jumps, or the HR Director asks why Venlo flex grew.
steps: Ask operations or finance for the volume picture, usually in Excel.
Download flex hours from the three agency portals and open roles from Recruitee.
Line them up by site and week in a spreadsheet.
Notice the peak after it has already become overtime and agency cost.
Mail a short note to the HR business partners. There is no standing monitor.
drudgery: Logging into three agency portals to download hour files
Client and site names that differ between AFAS, the site Excel and the agencies
Rebuilding the weekly comparison from scratch
Learning about a peak from the invoice, after the flex order is placed
today.time_sinks: The manual join across portals takes the time. The analyst often sees the peak about two weeks late, when the staffing and the 90-day outcome can no longer be shaped.

lenses.faster: A weekly table joins AFAS debtor revenue, agency hours and open roles by site, and the portal downloads and the paste-up fall away.
lenses.autonomous: When flex hours or open warehouse roles at a site move past a set band versus the recent average, the HR business partner and the analyst get a note that morning.
lenses.ambitious: HR sees a seasonal client peak in time to hire people who can still be productive and present at day 90, ahead of the week the extra containers arrive. The 150 to 300 flex workers become a planned response.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the portal downloads. What remains is the conversation with the site and the HR business partner about whether the peak is real and how to staff it.
lenses.options: A peak comes back as five staffing mixes: own-staff overtime, the current agencies, a different shift pattern, an earlier permanent hire, or declining the volume. Each shows cost, certificates needed, and CAO limits.
lenses.altitude: The analyst keeps the demand table, the name matching and the threshold. The site manager and the HR business partner decide how to staff.
reach: FP&A Analyst: the volume forecast that should feed this table
Controller: labour cost of own staff versus flex for the same peak
Recruiter: which peaks justify a permanent vacancy
HR Business Partner: the staffing conversation with the site manager

tasks.human_edge: Deciding with the site manager and the HR business partner whether a spike is a one-off, a new contract or a bad join. The client relationship stays with operations and finance.
tasks.pattern_why: Once debtor, agency hours and vacancies share a site and a week, the alert is a threshold on structured numbers. Where those names fail to match, the signal stays a conversation with the site manager.

in_practice.trigger: A weekly load of AFAS revenue, agency hours and Recruitee vacancies finishes, or a site crosses the agreed band.
steps: Load debtor revenue, agency hours and open roles onto one site-and-week table.
Flag rows where the client or site name failed to match.
Compare each site with its recent average and with the same week last season.
Draft a one-page note for the HR business partner: what moved, which source, and which open roles it touches.
Leave agency orders and vacancy approvals to the site and the recruiter.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases the weekly note until name matching has stayed clean for a quarter. Alerts that would lead to an agency order or a new vacancy always go through the HR business partner and the site.
data_needed: AFAS revenue by debtor and site
Weekly hours and cost from the three agencies
Open warehouse and driver roles from Recruitee
A site-level band agreed with the HR business partners
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint demand log: week, site, match rate, threshold breaches, and whether the note was released.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds debtor and sales data that a finance extract can already show.
Recruitee can list open vacancies by location and pipeline stage.
Three separate staffing-agency portals rarely share one clean client key with the finance ledger. The join often needs a mapping table.

risks: Client names do not match across AFAS, site spreadsheets and agency orders, and the monitor flags noise.
The analyst is pulled into commercial account work and away from day-90 retention and verzuim.
A demand note that names a client and a headcount plan reaches an agency and weakens Noordhaven's negotiating position.
Seasonal flex of 150 to 300 people swamps the signal and hides a permanent-hire problem.
research_questions: Can AFAS debtor revenue, agency hours and Recruitee vacancies be joined on site and week with a high match rate?
Who already forecasts warehouse volume, and does that forecast reach HR?
How many days before a flex spike does anyone in HR know about it today?
Would a wrong alert cause an agency order, or only a conversation?

tasks.short: Build the HR datasets and dashboards people actually use

today.trigger: The HR Director or an HR business partner asks for a view the current pack lacks, such as 90-day retention, Poortwachter deadlines, certificate compliance or time to hire.
steps: Turn the ask into fields, usually after two meetings.
Check whether AFAS, Recruitee or Studytube actually stores those fields.
Build a Power BI page or an Excel model and a draft definition.
Walk through it with the requester and correct the filters.
Publish to a small group and set access by hand.
drudgery: Rebuilding the site list, the date table and the contract-type filter for every new page
Discovering mid-build that week-one onboarding or productive at day 90 is not a field
Typing the access list by hand
Finishing a page that nobody opens
today.time_sinks: The slow part is the missing definition and the missing source field. Drawing the visual is the short part.

lenses.faster: A new page starts from the shared site, CAO, contract and date tables. AI drafts the model and the visual from the written definition, and the blank-file work drops out.
lenses.autonomous: When a North Star metric has no published tile, or a source gains a field the catalogue marked as needed, a draft workspace is opened for the analyst. Publishing stays a separate step.
lenses.ambitious: The four value streams get a proper tool for the first time: vacancy to day 90, the employee lifecycle under both CAOs, the Poortwachter timeline, and the payroll-close checks. More one-off Excel files are the wrong ambition.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the date and site scaffolding. The part people like is a page a shift manager will actually open on a Monday.
lenses.options: The same metric is drafted five ways before one is chosen: a site heatmap, a hire cohort, a Poortwachter aging list, an agency comparison and a board one-pager.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the standard: definition, test, access and owner. Generated pages are reviewed against that standard.
reach: FP&A Analyst: labour-cost pages built on the same populations
Payroll Specialist: control reports for the monthly pay run
Learning and Development Specialist: the mandatory-certificate board
Recruiter: a workbench on Recruitee stages and offer acceptance

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the question and the definition. A generated page that treats a proxy as productivity will be used as if the company had agreed it.
tasks.pattern_why: A coding agent can draft the dataset, the tests and the page from a written definition. The page counts when the analyst has checked the definition, the reconciliation and who can open it.

in_practice.trigger: A written request for a metric that the catalogue does not yet publish, tied to one of the four value streams.
steps: Write the definition, the population, the source field and the owner before any page is built.
Draft the dataset, the reconciliation test and up to five layouts in a workspace.
Reject the draft when the source field does not exist or the test misses a site.
The analyst and the metric owner pick one layout and set access.
Publish to the agreed audience and log the definition on SharePoint.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing is published until the analyst signs the definition, the reconciliation and the access list. A tool that monitors individual performance or predicts who will leave also needs works-council consent before build.
data_needed: Written metric definition and owner
Source field in AFAS, Recruitee or Studytube
Test totals by site
Audience and row-level security role
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint tool register: metric, owner, source, test result, access, publish date, and works-council status if it monitors staff.

evidence.claim: Coding assistants can draft SQL, a data model and a first report layout from a written spec, with a person checking the result.
AFAS Profit, Recruitee and Studytube are the source systems a new people-analytics tool at Noordhaven would have to use.
Works councils have consent rights over arrangements suitable for monitoring employee presence, behaviour or performance.
Recruitment, worker monitoring and decisions on terms of work are high-risk uses under the EU AI Act when a system scores individuals.

risks: A generated model drops a site or treats agency workers as Noordhaven employees.
A flight-risk or performance score is built as an ordinary dashboard and becomes a high-risk AI use that the works council has not consented to.
The page ships before the source field exists, and managers type their own numbers into it.
Access is copied from the last page and exposes wages or absence reasons.
research_questions: Which requested tools were abandoned, and was the cause a missing source field or a missing user?
Is there one shared dataset today, or a new Excel file per question?
Which proposed tools would monitor staff and need works-council consent before they are built?
How long did the last three dashboards take from the ask to first real use?

tasks.short: Compile hire, transfer, appraisal and absence figures

today.trigger: Month-end, a works-council meeting, a board pack, or a Poortwachter deadline asks for rates.
steps: Export hires, exits, transfers and absence from AFAS.
Add appraisal completion from AFAS when it is there, or collect it from the HR business partners.
Compute rates by site, sometimes with flex in and sometimes with flex out.
Look up individual records that make a rate look odd.
Paste the table into the board pack and the works-council pack.
drudgery: Recomputing a rate that AFAS already stores
Cleaning transfers that are really cost-centre corrections
Chasing appraisal spreadsheets from three HR business partners
Rebuilding verzuim with a slightly different denominator each month
today.time_sinks: The population rules take the time, especially absence and flex. Once the population is fixed, the arithmetic is short.

lenses.faster: The monthly statistical pack becomes a tested query. The export and the recomputation drop out.
lenses.autonomous: The pack runs when payroll locks, files itself, and flags a population that jumped: a missing site, flex doubled, or a transfer spike.
lenses.ambitious: Board, works council and payroll share one monthly series: hires, exits, internal moves, appraisal completion and verzuim, by site and contract, with flex shown separately. The series is on time every month.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the export cleanup. What remains is reading a real shift in absence or in exits before day 90, and the conversation that follows.
lenses.options: Every rate is shown for three populations side by side: own staff, own staff plus flex, and each CAO on its own.
lenses.altitude: The analyst locks the formulas and the population rules with payroll and the HR Director. HR admin continues to maintain the employee records in AFAS.
reach: Payroll Specialist: the joiner and leaver list that the pay run already needs
HR Business Partner: Poortwachter aging by deadline and site, limited to status and dates
Controller: the FTE bridge from the HR pack to the ledger
HR Administrator: the record corrections the pack keeps surfacing

tasks.human_edge: Reading what a movement means, and keeping medical judgment and individual performance stories out of the statistical pack. Corrections to records stay with HR admin and payroll.
tasks.pattern_why: Hires, transfers and absence hours are structured AFAS fields, and the rates are formulas. The pack is released when it matches the payroll population.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll lock for the month, or a works-council or Poortwachter date on the calendar.
steps: Run the agreed formulas for hires, exits, transfers, appraisal completion and verzuim on the payroll population.
Show own staff, flex and the two CAOs as separate columns.
Suppress groups under the agreed minimum size and omit absence reasons.
Flag records that moved the rate: a cost-centre fix coded as a transfer, a missing site, a long absence approaching the 42-week UWV notification.
File the pack for the board and, on the agreed dates, for the works council.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases a pack whose population does not match payroll, and any figure that will be sent to the works council or used in an UWV file. HR admin corrects the underlying record.
data_needed: AFAS movements, contract type, site and CAO
Absence hours on the payroll definition of verzuim
Appraisal completion, if it is stored
Poortwachter status dates, with medical content excluded
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint statistics log: month, population totals versus payroll, suppressed cells, and corrections sent to HR admin.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores contracts, absence and personnel movements and is the payroll source of record.
Wet verbetering poortwachter sets a reintegration file with fixed steps, including the 42-week notification to UWV. Status dates can be reported while medical content stays with the company doctor.
Dutch employers report a verzuim percentage to management, the works council and the arbodienst, and the denominator has to be the one payroll already uses.

risks: Someone treats the pack as a second personnel file and corrects employees in the dashboard.
A small Venlo team’s absence rate identifies a person. Health data is special-category data under the AVG.
Flex workers are employed by the agency. Mixing them into Noordhaven’s verzuim misstates the employer’s figure.
Appraisal completion is reported as if it were performance quality. It is only a process count.
The works council objects to a series it never agreed to receive.
research_questions: Are appraisals stored in AFAS, in Excel with the HR business partners, or inconsistently?
Which verzuim formula does payroll already use for the insurer and the works council, including partial return to work?
How many record corrections does HR admin make after the statistical pack is published?
Which series has the works council already agreed to receive?

tasks.short: Compare the labour market around the three sites with our own results

today.trigger: A compensation round, a hard-to-fill warehouse or driver role, an agency rate rise, or the CAO wage round.
steps: Look up regional figures and ask the agencies what they are seeing.
Compare CAO scales and allowances with what recruiters hear from candidates.
Pull Noordhaven time-to-fill, starter pay and 90-day exits by site from Recruitee and AFAS.
Write a mail or a few slides for the HR Director.
Compensation and the recruiters each keep their own version.
drudgery: Collecting the same regional wage and vacancy figures by hand each quarter
Copying CAO wage tables out of PDF
Rebuilding charts the compensation specialist already has
A slide that is stale before the management meeting
today.time_sinks: Gathering and lining up sources takes the time. The useful part is the comparison with Noordhaven’s own time-to-fill and 90-day outcomes.

lenses.faster: A quarterly pack lines up regional statistics, both CAO tables, agency rate cards and Noordhaven’s own hiring and 90-day results. Copying tables out of PDFs and old decks drops out.
lenses.autonomous: The pack refreshes on a quarterly date, when a new CAO table is filed on SharePoint, or when an agency rate card arrives. The analyst opens a prepared comparison.
lenses.ambitious: Each hard-to-fill role, such as forklift, reach truck, driver and team lead, has a living comparison for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, used before a vacancy has already sat for months.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses transcribing wage tables. What remains is the argument: pay, shift, certificate or the manager, and what Noordhaven is willing to change.
lenses.options: A tight site comes back as scenarios: pay at the CAO, an allowance, a different shift, a training route into the certificate, or more flex. Each shows cost, CAO and works-council constraints, and a range for time-to-fill.
lenses.altitude: The analyst keeps the source list and the comparison model. The meeting with Compensation, Recruiting and the HR Director is about the choice.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: the CAO and market comparison that feeds a pay proposal
Recruiter: the intake on a role that the market comparison says will not fill on the current shift and pay
FP&A Analyst: the labour-cost scenarios behind those options
HR Business Partner: advice to a site manager who wants to hire above the scale

tasks.human_edge: The recommendation touches pay, the CAO and often the works council. The HR Director and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist settle it. The analyst keeps every external figure tied to a source and a date.
tasks.pattern_why: CAO texts, UWV pages and agency mails are unstructured. The step that can be checked is a table with a source and a date on every figure. The pay and hiring choice stays with the HR Director and Compensation.

in_practice.trigger: The quarterly date arrives, a CAO file on SharePoint is replaced, or an agency sends a new rate card.
steps: Extract wage scales and allowances from the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO, each figure linked to the page it came from.
Add the latest CBS or UWV regional vacancy and wage figures for the three regions, with the period named.
Place Noordhaven time-to-fill, offer acceptance, starter pay and 90-day retention beside those figures, by role and site.
Draft scenarios with cost and with the inlenersbeloning constraint for flex. Leave a blank line where a figure has no source.
The analyst checks every number back to its source and then shares the pack.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the pack before it goes to the HR Director. Any figure without a source is removed. Pay proposals and works-council papers stay with Compensation and the HR Director.
data_needed: Current text of both CAOs
CBS or UWV figures for the three regions, with period
Agency rate cards, stored with restricted access
Internal time-to-fill, starter pay and 90-day retention by role and site
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint labour-market log: source, period, extractor, who checked the figures, and who received the pack.

evidence.claim: CBS StatLine and UWV publish regional labour-market and vacancy statistics that can be cited with a period.
Recruitee and AFAS Profit hold internal time-to-fill, offers and starter records.
A language model can lift a wage table from a CAO PDF into rows, and every cell still has to be checked against the PDF.

risks: A drafted market rate above the CAO creates a pay expectation the CAO or the works council will not support. Transport and warehouse scales get mixed.
External job titles do not match the jobs Noordhaven uses on the floor, so the comparison looks tighter or looser than it is.
Agency rate cards are commercially sensitive and leak if the pack is posted to a wide Teams channel.
The pack slides into ranking candidates. Used that way it can be a high-risk system under the EU AI Act. It has to stay a market comparison.
A wage figure is invented where the PDF was unclear. Every number needs a source line.
research_questions: Which external sources do Compensation and the recruiters already trust, and how often are they refreshed?
Can both CAO wage tables and the main allowances be extracted with every figure checked back to the PDF?
For which roles is the binding constraint pay, a certificate, the shift, or the manager?
Did the last four market notes change a pay or hiring decision, or were they filed unread?

role.altitude: The analyst owns the definitions, the tests, the access rules and the calendar of HR numbers. Site managers, payroll, finance and the works council work from one population for hiring, day-90 retention, verzuim, certificates and the pay cycle. The analyst spends the week on breaks, definition changes and the pattern behind the North Star.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pre-lock checks on joiners, leavers and new CAO wage components
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: sourced CAO and regional pay comparisons for both CAOs
Recruiter: Recruitee funnel definitions, time to hire and offer acceptance
Learning and Development Specialist: Studytube certificate expiry for forklift, VCA and food safety
FP&A Analyst and Controller: the labour-cost and FTE bridge from the HR population to the ledger
HR Administrator: the AFAS field rules that keep the extract clean, while data entry stays there
HR Business Partner: Poortwachter aging by deadline and site, limited to status and dates
role.ceiling_note: This is one FTE, about 1,600 hours a year, at a loaded cost of EUR 78 an hour. The eight tasks here are a bit over half of that year and are the part that can shrink. The ceiling on the rest is source quality, three agency portals that do not share a client key, and decisions this role must not take: pay, dismissal, medical judgment, and works-council consent. One analyst can run the reporting system. They cannot also be the three HR business partners on the warehouse floor.
skills_to_grow: The AFAS Profit model and the nightly extract, including payroll components for both CAOs
Metric design for verzuim, flex versus own staff, and productive at day 90, written so payroll, a site manager and the works council can all use it
Power BI modeling, row-level security and reconciliation tests
Enough SQL or Python to keep those tests in code
Judgment on when a people report becomes staff monitoring or a high-risk use under the EU AI Act
role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven runs one people-and-labour picture. Every open role is visible through to day 90, every long absence has a Poortwachter clock that HR acts on before the UWV deadline, every mandatory certificate is current before the shift, and payroll, finance and the works council use the same populations. Packs arrive on the calendar. The analyst’s week goes to the hiring or absence pattern that is actually moving the North Star, and to the definition changes the company still has to agree.
